Modbus/TCP incident at IED1A, a field device (Modbus server) (b1): 2 anomalous 10-second windows over 1 minute. Per 10-second window, at most: read requests 11-100, write requests 0, requests with other function codes 0, exception responses 0; request rate normal. Observed: requests from a peer never seen in training; requests to register addresses never seen in training; requests for more values than ever seen in training. Deviating counters: frames whose length field does not match their content, or truncated frames (malformed_frames) fell, high deviation; requests for more values than any request seen in training (oversized_qty) rose, high deviation; requests with other function codes (req_other) fell, high deviation; requests that received no response (unanswered) rose, high deviation; requests to register addresses never seen in training (unseen_addr) rose, high deviation.

On the boiler side, the return tank level climbed sharply while the LCV01 level valve was driven further open and its position followed; inflow measured at FT01 dropped and outlet pressure sagged. A valve demand that never moves in normal running (PCV2) also shifted.

Node a2 flagged five minutes of abnormal boiler behaviour: tank level up, level valve demand and feedback up, flow and heat-exchanger pressure down, plus an unexpected change on a normally fixed valve demand.
Return tank level fell even though the level valve was driven more open; the level target for that tank itself moved upward, and the normally static PCV2 valve demand changed.
Eight minutes of boiler anomalies on a2: the level target went up, the level control valve opened, flow rose and the tank level dropped.
Short boiler disturbance on a1: inflow readings jumped while outflow readings and the FCV03 valve position dropped, with no target or demand change visible.

Turbine speed probes on a3 read lower, shaft displacement shifted on both axes and the key phasor lag dropped; the emergency button and the turbine on/off switch, which never change normally, both changed state.
Two minutes of turbine trouble: falling RPM, changed shaft displacement near the first mass wheel, and unexpected toggling of the emergency and on/off controls.
The turbine slowed according to its speed probes, displacement readings near the first wheel moved, and the emergency and run switches changed although they are fixed in normal operation.
The speed controller's output dropped and the turbine RPM followed it down; phasor lag and shaft displacement also moved, and the normally fixed emergency and on/off inputs changed.
On a1 the turbine governor output fell, speed decreased, and switches that never move in routine running flipped.
Turbine speed control output went down together with RPM, and Y-axis shaft displacement dropped near both mass wheels.
Both turbine and boiler were disturbed on a1: turbine speed fell while boiler inflow and the FCV03 valve opening rose, and the emergency and power switches changed state.
Four minutes in which RPM dropped, phasor lag fell, boiler flow increased and two normally constant turbine switches were altered.
The level valve was told to open further and did, heat-exchanger pressure rose, boiler inflow fell and the FCV03 valve closed somewhat.
a4 saw four minutes where the LCV01 demand and position went up together with outlet pressure, while flow and FCV03 position went down.
The FCV03 valve was driven closed and followed, tank level and flow dropped, the level valve moved open, and the static PCV2 valve demand changed.
Boiler on a2: falling level and flow while the flow valve demand dropped; a normally constant valve demand also moved.
The FCV03 valve demand rose and its position followed, but measured inflow went down; the LCV01 valve position also increased.
Two minutes of boiler anomaly on a1, with a higher flow-valve demand and reduced inflow.
Seven minutes on a3: level valve demand and feedback climbed, inflow and outlet pressure rose, outflow dropped.
The boiler's level valve was pushed open for several minutes, with more water coming in, higher heat-exchanger pressure and less going out.
Turbine governor output fell on a2 and the shaft slowed; displacement and phasor signals moved and the emergency and on/off inputs changed.
Speed control output decreased, RPM dropped, and normally fixed turbine safety switches were toggled.
A host that had never talked to IED1A before sent it read requests for registers outside its usual range, including one asking for far more values than normal; some requests went unanswered.
Unknown client polling the field device with an oversized read and unfamiliar register addresses, no writes.
A new peer sent IED1A input-register reads at a high rate, packed several Modbus frames into one packet, sent frames with broken lengths and asked for unusually large blocks.
Three minutes of strange reads against the IED from an unfamiliar host, with bundled frames, wrong length fields and oversize requests.
An unfamiliar host read from IED1A across register ranges it has never accessed, asking for more data than usual, without writing anything.
Brief burst of reads from a previously unseen client against unfamiliar addresses on the IED, one request asking for an unusually large amount of data.
IED1A answered a couple of out-of-pattern read requests from a newcomer on the network; nothing was written.
